Imperial Japan. The Japanese nation during the period of rapid industrialization and imperial expansion from the Meiji Restoration of eighteen-sixty-eight through World War Two. Driven by nationalist ideology and a desire for continental power, Japan transformed into a militaristic state that sought dominance over East Asia. This era fundamentally reshaped the region's geopolitics and left a legacy of conflict and suffering.

Japan rose rapidly to great-power status after the Meiji Restoration embraced Western technology and military reforms, transforming a feudal society into an industrial military power within decades. The nation built a powerful navy and army, defeating the Russian Empire in the Russo-Japanese War from nineteen-oh-four to nineteen-oh-five and gaining respect as a military power. This was the first time an Asian nation defeated a European power, shocking the global order.

Japan pursued expansionism across East Asia: captured Korea in nineteen-ten and annexed it, invaded Manchuria in nineteen-thirty-one, and waged the Second Sino-Japanese War against China from nineteen-thirty-seven to nineteen-forty-five, killing millions of Chinese civilians. The government became increasingly militaristic, with military factions gaining dominance over civilian politics through the nineteen-twenties and nineteen-thirties. They assassinated moderate politicians to impose military control.

Japan allied with Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy in the Axis pact of nineteen-thirty-six, viewing the alliance as serving its imperial ambitions in Asia while Germany expanded in Europe. Japan initiated the Pacific War by attacking Pearl Harbor on December seventh, nineteen-forty-one, destroying American battleships and bringing the United States into World War Two. Japan surrendered unconditionally in September nineteen-forty-five after atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, totaling approximately two hundred thousand immediate deaths plus hundreds of thousands more from radiation sickness. The nation was subsequently occupied and democratized by American forces under General Douglas MacArthur.
